## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Saraṇaduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 15.70) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka. Bibliographically classified as a leaf section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the text treats the analytical intersection of the *saraṇaduka* (the dyad regarding defilement or corrupting influence) with the foundational *kusalattika* (the triad of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena) within the system of conditional relations (paccaya).

 Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus confirms the absence of substantial cross-language alignments with a score of 10 or greater, but identifies 219 Pali-internal matching passages shared with 59 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. These matches reflect extensive repetitive structural reuse across other permutations in the *Paṭṭhāna*, most prominently sharing significant passages with *Kusalattika, Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 4.7, e.g., §3.1_2–5.1 ↔ §127.1–129.1), *Kusalattika, Tika* (Patthana 5.1), *Saraṇaduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.14), *Tika Saraṇaduka* (Patthana 4.8), and *Piṭṭhiduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 21.16) [DharmaNexus].
